title: Publication Data Cleaning in Excel for Author Name Gender Analysis
author: Stephen W Gabrielson
materials: Select Delimited and then click Next .
There should now be two columns.
Select the column containing author names.
Select the First Name column on the right.
Choose your settings in these next steps.
Select Keep existing columns under Global settings .
Review your data before processing your file.

steps.title: Export Publication Data from Dimensions
steps.instruction: Export publication records as a CSV file from the Dimensions Free Web App.

substeps.instruction: Access the Free Web App and log in or register for a personal account.
Limit results to a specific journal by expanding the 'Source Title' filter, typing the full journal name (no abbreviations), and clicking 'Limit to'.
Further limit results by 'Publication Year' if necessary to stay within the 2500 record export limit for free accounts.
Click 'Save / Export' to the right of the search box and select 'Export results'.
Choose the export option for 'bibliometric mapping' and click 'Export'.
Navigate to the 'Export center' via the account profile name in the upper right corner.
Download the ZIP file containing the CSV publication data.
If combining multiple export files, delete the first two rows of subsequent files before merging into the main CSV.

steps.title: Initial Spreadsheet Preparation
steps.instruction: Prepare the raw CSV data in Excel for cleaning.

substeps.instruction: Open the CSV file in Excel and delete the first row starting with 'about this data'.
Save the original spreadsheet with a descriptive name (e.g., dimensions_original_year).
Review the file for erroneous data caused by Excel's 32,767 character cell limit; delete these rows or use a text editor/Google Sheets if this occurs.
Copy and paste the 'Authors' column into a new spreadsheet named descriptively (e.g., authors_year).

steps.title: Separate Authors into Columns
steps.instruction: Split the semicolon-separated author lists into individual columns.

substeps.instruction: Go to the 'Data' tab and select 'Text to Columns'.
Uncheck 'Tab' and select 'Semicolon' as the delimiter.
Leave 'General' selected and click 'Finish'.

steps.title: Extract First and Last Authors
steps.instruction: Isolate the first and last authors from the expanded author list.

substeps.instruction: Rename the first author column to 'First Authors'.
Create an empty column named 'Last Authors' at the end of the spreadsheet.

In row 2 of the 'Last Authors' column, enter the formula: =IF(B2<>"",LOOKUP(2,1/(A2:YOURCOLUMNHERE2<>""),A2:YOURCOLUMNHERE2),""), replacing 'YOURCOLUMNHERE' with the column letter immediately to the left of the Last Authors column.
Select the cell with the formula and the remaining cells in the 'Last Authors' column, then go to 'Home' > 'Fill' > 'Down'.
Convert the 'Last Authors' formulas to values to prevent data loss when deleting middle columns: use 'Alt + E + S + V' or 'Home' > 'Paste' > 'Paste values'.
Delete the middle author columns.

steps.title: Remove Blank Rows
steps.instruction: Clean the author spreadsheets by removing rows without author data.

substeps.instruction: Go to 'Home' > 'Find & Select' > 'Blanks' and click 'OK'.
Go to 'Home' > 'Delete' (dropdown) > 'Delete Cells' > 'Entire row'.
Note: If using 'Text to Columns' as a precursor, select 'Delimited' and click 'Finish'.

steps.title: Create Individual Author Files
steps.instruction: Split the first and last authors into separate files for analysis.

substeps.instruction: Copy and paste the 'First Authors' column (including header) into a new spreadsheet saved as 'first_authors_year'.
Copy and paste the 'Last Authors' column (including header) into a new spreadsheet saved as 'last_authors_year'.
Remove any blank rows from the 'last_authors_year' file using the blank row removal method described previously.

steps.title: Clean Author Name Formatting
steps.instruction: Standardize names by separating first and last names and removing initials.

substeps.instruction: Perform the following for both 'first_authors_year' and 'last_authors_year' files:
Go to 'Data' > 'Text to Columns', select 'Comma' as the delimiter, and click 'Finish'.
Rename the resulting columns to 'Last Name' and 'First Name'.
To remove middle initials: Go to 'Data' > 'Text to Columns', select 'Space' as the delimiter, and click 'Finish'.
Remove the empty whitespace column and rename columns if necessary, ensuring names like 'Mary Lou' are not accidentally split and that names formatted as 'M. Elizabeth' are corrected.
Review names for special characters (e.g., §, Ã, ©, ?) and correct spellings by referencing the original Dimensions spreadsheet and the web app.
Use the 'Replace' option in 'Find & Select' to make corrections.

steps.title: Analyze Gender with Namsor
steps.instruction: Upload the cleaned files to Namsor to determine gender, origin, and ethnicity.

substeps.instruction: Log in to Namsor and click 'Excel/CSV' to upload the file (supported formats: .xls, .xlsx, .csv, .txt, .ods; files <3MB recommended).
Click 'Validate files'.
Select the feature 'Genderize Name: gender from first name, last name (optional)' and click 'Choose this feature'.
Select 'The file has a header' and confirm 'First row = 2'.
Identify the first name and last name columns under 'Column settings' and click 'Validate settings'.
Review the summary chart, click 'The data looks good', and review the final summary and credit cost.
Click 'Process file' and download the generated file, reviewing the 'likelyGender' column for results.
